title: "Elastic net on traits, everyone pooled"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true

  echo: true
  warning: false
---

Which proteins, modules or Hallmark sets, taken together, carry information about muscle size and
strength? An elastic net is a regression with a penalty on the size of its weights: the lasso part
sets most weights to zero, so the model keeps a short list of features, and the ridge part shares
weight among correlated features instead of picking one at random (Zou and Hastie 2005). With 16
people and up to 2,059 proteins the fit cannot be a predictor for new people; it is used here to
find features that carry a trait jointly, read with care. No group label enters any model.

Six pairings of a feature value with a trait, per person:

| Pairing | Features | Trait |
|---|---|---|
| T1 level vs T1 trait | T1 level | T1 level |
| T1 level predicts gain | T1 level | % gain, growth score |
| training change tracks gain | T2 − T1 | % gain, growth score |
| T2 level vs T2 trait | T2 level | T2 level |
| acute change vs T2 trait | T3 − T2 | T2 level |
| acute change vs gain | T3 − T2 | % gain, growth score |

There is no phenotype at T3. The bout falls in trained muscle, so its response is set against the
trained trait levels and the gain already made.

## Packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
source(here("02_HRvLR", "helpers.R"))
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
inputs <- c(
  corrected = "01_Processing/03_Blood_Correction/c_data/proteins_corrected.rds",
  modules = "01_Processing/06_Module_Building/c_data/modules.rds",
  singscore = "01_Processing/05_Set_Scores/c_data/singscore.rds",
  gene_sets = "01_Processing/04_Gene_Sets/c_data/gene_sets.rds",
  phenotype = "00_Setup/Input/phenotype.csv"
)
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
```

## Input

Three feature sets per person: blood-corrected proteins, module eigengenes and the qualifying
Hallmark set scores. A feature with no spread across the 16 people in a window (one modelled value
for everyone) is left out of that window.

```{r}
#| label: input
corrected <- readRDS(paths[["corrected"]])
modules <- readRDS(paths[["modules"]])
scores <- readRDS(paths[["singscore"]])$scores
gs <- readRDS(paths[["gene_sets"]])
phenotype <- readr::read_csv(paths[["phenotype"]], show_col_types = FALSE)
meta <- as_tibble(corrected$targets)
hallmark <- filter(gs$set_catalog, collection == "Hallmark", qualifies)$set_id
label_of <- c(
  set_names(sub(";.*", "", corrected$genes$Genes), rownames(corrected)),
  set_names(sub("^Hallmark\\|HALLMARK_", "", hallmark), hallmark),
  set_names(rownames(modules$eigengenes))
)
feature_sets <- list(
  proteins = corrected$E, modules = modules$eigengenes, hallmark = scores[hallmark, meta$sample_id]
)
x_of <- function(values, window) {
  m <- switch(window,
    T1 = person_values(values, meta, "T1"), T2 = person_values(values, meta, "T2"),
    training = person_values(values, meta, "T2", from = "T1"),
    acute = person_values(values, meta, "T3", from = "T2")
  )
  x <- t(m)
  x[, apply(x, 2, sd) > 0, drop = FALSE]
}
traits <- trait_windows(phenotype)
levels_at <- c("fcsa_mixed", "mcsa", "leg_press_1rm", "leg_ext_1rm")
gains <- c(paste0("pct_", levels_at), "comp_hypertrophy")
fits <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    pairing = "T1 level vs T1 trait", window = "T1", table = "baseline_level", trait = levels_at
  ),
  tibble(pairing = "T1 level predicts gain", window = "T1", table = "training", trait = gains),
  tibble(
    pairing = "training change tracks gain", window = "training", table = "training",
    trait = gains
  ),
  tibble(pairing = "T2 level vs T2 trait", window = "T2", table = "post_level", trait = levels_at),
  tibble(
    pairing = "acute change vs T2 trait", window = "acute", table = "post_level",
    trait = levels_at
  ),
  tibble(pairing = "acute change vs gain", window = "acute", table = "training", trait = gains)
) |>
  expand_grid(features = names(feature_sets))
nrow(fits)
```

## Two readings per fit

**Which features carry the trait (stability selection; Meinshausen and Bühlmann 2010).** On each
of 200 random subsamples of 12 people, the elastic net (α = 0.5) keeps the first q features to
enter its path. A feature's selection frequency is the share of subsamples that keep it. With
q = min(20, max(1, ⌊√(0.2 p)⌋)) for p features (20 for proteins, 1 for the 10 modules, 2 for the
35 Hallmark sets), the expected number of features kept in at least 60% of subsamples by chance
alone is at most q² / ((2 × 0.6 − 1) p), below 1 in every fit. Two exploratory tiers:
stable (≥ 0.6, the bound applies) and recurring (0.4 to 0.6, a lead without a bound).

**How well the features predict held-out people (Q²).** Four-fold cross-validation repeated 5
times, λ chosen by 3-fold cross-validation inside each training set; Q² = 1 − held-out error /
error of predicting each held-out person by the training mean, so Q² ≤ 0 means no better than the
mean. The null reruns it on 1,000 shuffles of the trait (2 repeats each); p = (1 + null ≥ observed)
/ 1,001. A fit at p < 0.10 is a lead; with 81 fits, about 8 leads are expected from chance alone.
Each person's held-out prediction, averaged over the 5 repeats, is kept for the figure.

```{r}
#| label: fits
stability <- function(x, y, q, subsamples = 200, size = 12) {
  kept <- replicate(subsamples, {
    rows <- sample(nrow(x), size)
    path <- glmnet::glmnet(x[rows, ], y[rows], alpha = 0.5)
    first <- which(path$df >= q)[1]
    if (is.na(first)) first <- length(path$lambda)
    rownames(path$beta)[path$beta[, first] != 0]
  }, simplify = FALSE)
  map_dbl(colnames(x), \(f) mean(map_lgl(kept, \(k) f %in% k)))
}
held_out <- function(x, y, repeats) {
  preds <- map(seq_len(repeats), \(r) {
    folds <- sample(rep_len(1:4, length(y)))
    pred <- base <- numeric(length(y))
    for (f in 1:4) {
      train <- folds != f
      fit <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(x[train, ], y[train], alpha = 0.5, nfolds = 3)
      pred[!train] <- predict(fit, x[!train, , drop = FALSE], s = "lambda.min")
      base[!train] <- mean(y[train])
    }
    list(q2 = 1 - sum((y - pred)^2) / sum((y - base)^2), pred = pred)
  })
  list(q2 = mean(map_dbl(preds, "q2")), pred = rowMeans(sapply(preds, `[[`, "pred")))
}

RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")
set.seed(20261030)
n_perm <- 1000
results <- parallel::mclapply(seq_len(nrow(fits)), \(i) {
  s <- fits[i, ]
  x_all <- x_of(feature_sets[[s$features]], s$window)
  table <- traits[[s$table]]
  y_all <- table[[s$trait]][match(rownames(x_all), table$subject)]
  x <- x_all[!is.na(y_all), ]
  y <- y_all[!is.na(y_all)]
  q <- min(20, max(1, floor(sqrt(0.2 * ncol(x)))))
  frequency <- stability(x, y, q)
  held <- held_out(x, y, 5)
  null <- replicate(n_perm, held_out(x, sample(y), 2)$q2)
  list(
    summary = bind_cols(s, tibble(
      n_people = length(y), n_features = ncol(x), q,
      false_bound = q^2 / ((2 * 0.6 - 1) * ncol(x)), q2 = held$q2,
      null_median = median(null), null_95 = unname(quantile(null, 0.95)),
      p_perm = (1 + sum(null >= held$q2)) / (1 + n_perm)
    )),
    selection = bind_cols(s[rep(1, ncol(x)), ], tibble(
      feature = colnames(x), frequency,
      rho = apply(x, 2, \(v) cor(v, y, method = "spearman"))
    )),
    predictions = bind_cols(s[rep(1, length(y)), ], tibble(
      subject = rownames(x), observed = y, predicted = held$pred
    ))
  )
}, mc.cores = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1), mc.set.seed = TRUE)

selection <- list_rbind(map(results, "selection")) |>
  mutate(
    label = unname(label_of[feature]),
    tier = case_when(frequency >= 0.6 ~ "stable", frequency >= 0.4 ~ "recurring", .default = "rare")
  )
summary <- list_rbind(map(results, "summary")) |>
  left_join(
    summarise(selection,
      n_stable = sum(tier == "stable"), n_recurring = sum(tier == "recurring"),
      .by = c(pairing, trait, features)
    ),
    by = c("pairing", "trait", "features")
  )
predictions <- list_rbind(map(results, "predictions")) |>
  left_join(distinct(meta, subject, group), by = "subject")
selection <- filter(selection, tier != "rare")
summary |>
  arrange(p_perm) |>
  select(pairing, trait, features, q2, p_perm, n_stable, n_recurring) |>
  head(10)
```

## What the selected proteins are

Over-representation (clusterProfiler, the `07_Module_Characterisation` settings) of each fit's
stable and recurring proteins against the measured genes; an exploratory lead at FDR < 0.10.

```{r}
#| label: ora
term2gene <- enframe(gs$sets, "set_id", "gene") |> unnest(gene)
selection_ora <- selection |>
  filter(features == "proteins") |>
  summarise(genes = list(unique(na.omit(label))), .by = c(pairing, trait)) |>
  filter(lengths(genes) >= 4) |>
  pmap(\(pairing, trait, genes) {
    e <- clusterProfiler::enricher(genes,
      TERM2GENE = term2gene, universe = gs$gene_universe,
      minGSSize = 15, maxGSSize = 500, pvalueCutoff = 1, qvalueCutoff = 1
    )
    if (is.null(e)) {
      return(NULL)
    }
    as_tibble(as.data.frame(e)) |>
      slice_min(p.adjust, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |>
      transmute(pairing, trait, set_id = ID, overlap = GeneRatio, p = pvalue, fdr = p.adjust)
  }) |>
  list_rbind()
filter(selection_ora, fdr < 0.10)
```

## Validation

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  nrow(summary) == nrow(fits), all(summary$p_perm > 0 & summary$p_perm <= 1),
  all(summary$false_bound <= 1), !anyNA(predictions$predicted),
  all(between(selection$frequency, 0.4, 1))
)
```

## Summary

`r sum(summary$p_perm < 0.10)` of `r nrow(summary)` fits are leads at permutation p < 0.10
(about `r round(0.10 * nrow(summary))` expected by chance). The strongest is
`r with(slice_min(summary, p_perm, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE), sprintf("%s, %s, %s: Q2 %.2f, p %.3f", pairing, trait, features, q2, p_perm))`.

## Save

```{r}
#| label: save
out <- here("03_Continuous", "04_Elastic_Net", "c_data")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
saved <- list(
  summary = summary, selection = selection, selection_ora = selection_ora,
  predictions = predictions
)
saveRDS(saved, file.path(out, "elastic_net.rds"))
write_workbook(
  saved,
  c(
    "Per fit (pairing, trait, feature set): held-out Q2, its permutation null, stable counts.",
    "Per fit and feature selected in >= 40% of subsamples: frequency, tier, Spearman rho.",
    "Per fit: top over-represented sets among its selected proteins.",
    "Per fit and person: observed trait and held-out prediction (mean over 5 repeats)."
  ),
  file.path(out, "elastic_net.xlsx"), inputs, paths
)
```
